For me Irony is more like this definition

"a state of affairs or an event that seems deliberately contrary to what one expects and is often amusing as a result."

The first definition which you have is more like sarcasm

"the expression of one's meaning by using language that normally signifies the opposite, typically for humorous or emphatic effect."

EDIT: EX,

Irony is usually for me a good/bad scale. Like you going to a friend to talk and make you feel better and they end up making you feel worse "the irony is that I thought he could help me"

Sarcasm is the same place would be like " Oh thanks so much for the help it really cheered me up"

Sarcasm is where you say something but mean the opposite.

  • Atko isn't gay at all

Irony is a little harder to define. It's usually something funny that is also coincidental.

  • "Yeah, apparently he was hit by an ambulance in a graveyard"
Would you also agree this would be irony "to think ambulances try to keep you out of a graveyard"

I think the vast majority of the time the irony isn't found in what you're saying, it's in the event/idea you're describing. Contrast and contradiction are what make up irony. An example of contrast would be the ambulance/graveyard analogy, because it is highlighting the contrast between life/death. An example of contradiction would be a scandal where an anti-gay marriage politician's gay orgy sex tape surfaced online. You can say something ironic, but the irony is that you contradicted a previous statement, or you can describe an ironic idea/event, it isn't found in the words. I think that's what separates it from sarcasm, because sarcasm is all about the words.

It is thought in the UK that Americans aren't as good at perceiving irony, or getting the definition right. I think the reason for this is the difference in our comedy/humour, irony is a main theme in British comedy, but America tends to take things to a ridiculous or extreme place to find the laugh. Both can be hilarious, but some British people don't like American comedy as much because it's seen as being cheap or unclever sometimes.

Use Signal. It is open source, highly maintained, works on android, ios, and soon as a chrome/chromium extension (currently in public beta). End to end encryption for all texts, calls, pictures, videos, etc., is the default, no need to create a "private" conversation like what Telegram does, all your conversations are private. However, Signal does allow you to send unencrypted messages to friends who do not have the app.

Other options that could theoretically work but you will never get your friends to use: ChatSecure (drops too many messages/ unusable), PGP (your friends will not be able to figure it out), Pond (not well tested enough, too technical to set up)

Non options: do not use Telegram, Threema, Sicher, WhatsApp, Skype, Hangouts, Viber, Trillian, Empathy, Nimbuzz, IM+, Linphone, WeChat, KIK, or any other closed source or partially closed source messaging application. Security through obscurity does not and cannot work, and "custom crypto" is a huge red flag. Only use well known time tested and critically reviewed fully open source code.
